title: A mother’s gift: Provisioning of plastid-derived structures into eggs promotes invertebrate development and dispersal
content:
by Jillian P. Lewis, Spencer V. Nyholm

Eggs released in the environment are at risk from many threats. A recent study in PLOS Biology reveals that plastid-derived carotenoid crystals in sea urchin eggs benefit larval survival and trans-oceanic dispersal. Eggs released in the environment are at risk from many threats. This Primer discusses how plastid-like carotenoid crystals benefit larval survival and trans-oceanic dispersal in sea urchin eggs.
author: Jillian P. Lewis
